{{short description|American basketball player (born 2002)}} {{Use mdy dates|date=July 2023}} {{Use American English|date=July 2023}} {{Infobox basketball biography | name = Grant Nelson | image = Grant Nelson.jpg | caption = Nelson with [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]] in 2024 | birth_date = {{birth date and age|2002|3|18}} | birth_place = [[Devils Lake, North Dakota]], U.S. | height_ft = 7 | height_in = 0 | weight_lbs = 215 | league = [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] | team = Brooklyn Nets | position = [[Power forward]] | number = 16 | high_school = [[Devils Lake High School|Devils Lake]]
(Devils Lake, North Dakota) | college = * [[North Dakota State Bison men's basketball|North Dakota State]] (2020–2023) * [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]] (2023–2025) | draft_year = 2025 | career_start = 2025 | years1 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2025-2026]] | team1 = [[Long Island Nets]] | years2 = {{nbay|2025|end}}–present | team2 = [[Brooklyn Nets]] | years3 = [[2026–27 NBA G League season|2026]]–present | team3 = →Long Island Nets | highlights = * First team All-[[Summit League]] ([[2022–23 Summit League men's basketball season|2023]]) * Summit League All-Defensive Team (2023) * Summit League Sixth Man of the Year ([[2020–21 Summit League men's basketball season|2021]]) * [[North Dakota Mr. Basketball]] (2020) }} '''Grant Nelson''' (born March 18, 2002) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Brooklyn Nets]] of the National Basketball Association (NBA), on a two-way contract with the [[Long Island Nets]] of the NBA G League. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama Crimson Tide]] and the [[North Dakota State Bison men's basketball|North Dakota State Bison]]. ==Early life and high school career== Nelson grew up in [[Devils Lake, North Dakota]] and attended [[Devils Lake High School]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4206199/2023/02/22/victor-wembanyama-height-weight-prospect-nba-draft/|title=The Unicorn Era: Victor Wembanyama heads a coming stampede of skilled big men|first=Seth|last=Davis|website=[[The Athletic]]|date=February 22, 2023|access-date=February 28, 2023}} He played mostly on the junior varsity team as a freshman and sophomore.{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/north-dakota-state/Article/NDSU-Basketball-Head-Coach-David-Richman-Offers-Two-Big-Men-133002434/|title=Bison Hoops Offers Two Big Men|first=Nate|last=Zastrow|website=[[247Sports]]|date=June 20, 2019|access-date=February 28, 2023}} Nelson averaged 16.4 points, 11.5 rebounds, and 5.1 blocks per game and was named second team All-State during his junior season.{{cite web|url=https://www.grandforksherald.com/sports/devils-lakes-grant-nelson-standing-out-above-the-basketball-crowd|title=Devils Lake's Grant Nelson standing out above the basketball crowd|work=[[Grand Forks Herald]]|date=December 24, 2019|access-date=February 28, 2023}} He was named [[North Dakota Mr. Basketball]] as a senior after averaging 25 points, 18 rebounds, and 5.7 blocks per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.inforum.com/grant-nelson-wins-mr-basketball|title=Devils Lake's Nelson named North Dakota Mr. Basketball|work=[[The Forum of Fargo-Moorhead]]|date=March 27, 2020|access-date=February 28, 2023}} Nelson committed to playing college basketball for [[North Dakota State Bison men's basketball|North Dakota State]] over offers from [[North Dakota Fighting Hawks men's basketball|North Dakota]] and [[NCAA Division II|Division II]] programs [[Northern State Wolves#Men's basketball|Northern State]], [[Mary Marauders|University of Mary]], [[Minot State Beavers|Minot State]], and [[Minnesota State–Moorhead Dragons#Men's basketball|Minnesota State-Moorhead]].{{cite web|url=https://www.grandforksherald.com/sports/devils-lakes-grant-nelson-to-play-college-basketball-at-ndsu|title=Devils Lake's Grant Nelson to play college basketball at NDSU|work=[[Grand Forks Herald]]|date=July 8, 2019|access-date=February 28, 2023}} ==College career== ===North Dakota State=== Nelson played in all 27 of NDSU's games, with five starts as a freshman and was named the [[Summit League]] Sixth Man of the Year after averaging 6.3 points and 3.7 rebounds per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.inforum.com/sports/bison-media-zone/mens-sports/with-grant-nelson-bison-men-have-a-unique-player-to-throw-at-opposing-teams|title=With Grant Nelson, Bison men have a unique player to throw at opposing teams|work=[[The Forum of Fargo-Moorhead]]|date=October 31, 2021|access-date=February 28, 2023}} He became a starter as a sophomore and averaged 11.6 points and 4.9 rebounds per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.inforum.com/sports/bison-media-zone/mens-sports/bison-forward-maleeck-harden-hayes-enters-the-transfer-portal|title=Bison men's basketball players Cook, Harden-Hayes enter the transfer portal|work=[[The Forum of Fargo-Moorhead]]|date=March 14, 2022|access-date=February 28, 2023}}{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/nba/draft/prospect-profiles/nba-draft-scouting-report-north-dakota-states-grant-nelson|title=NBA Draft Scouting Report: North Dakota State's Grant Nelson|website=[[SI.com]]|date=February 25, 2023|access-date=February 28, 2023}} During Nelson's junior season, a highlight reel of his play went [[Viral video|viral]] in early January 2023.{{cite web|url=https://www.inforum.com/sports/bison-media-zone/mens-sports/mcfeely-thanks-in-part-to-viral-video-nba-draft-steam-begins-for-bisons-grant-nelson|title=McFeely: Thanks in part to viral video, NBA steam begins for Bison's Grant Nelson|work=[[The Forum of Fargo-Moorhead]]|date=January 13, 2023|access-date=February 28, 2023}} As a junior, Grant averaged 17.9 points and 9.3 rebounds per game, as well as shooting 52.1% from the field.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/player/_/id/4702670/grant-nelson|title=Grant Nelson Stats, News, Bio|website=espn.com|publisher=ESPN|access-date=March 3, 2023}} These stats also earned him his first All-Summit First Team and All-Summit Defensive Team honors.{{cite web|url=https://thesummitleague.org/news/2023/3/2/awards-orus-abmas-nets-second-summitmbb-player-of-the-year-award.aspx|title=ORU's Abmas nets second #SummitMBB Player of the Year Award|website=thesummitleague.org|publisher=The Summit League|date=March 2, 2023|access-date=March 3, 2023}} ===Alabama=== Following the 2022–23 season, Nelson explored his options in the [[2023 NBA draft]] but ultimately withdrew to return to college for his senior season. On June 12, 2023, he transferred to [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]] after spending three seasons at North Dakota State.{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4601196/2023/06/12/grant-nelson-alabama-basketball/|title=North Dakota State transfer Grant Nelson commits to Alabama: What Tide are getting in big man|website=theathletic.com|publisher=The Athletic|date=June 12, 2023|access-date=July 11, 2023}} Nelson averaged 11.9 points, 5.9 rebounds, and 1.6 blocks per game for the [[2023–24 Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball team|Crimson Tide in 2023-24]]. In the Sweet 16 of the [[2024 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2024 NCAA Tournament]] against [[2023–24 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]], he posted 24 points, 12 rebounds, and 5 blocks, helping Alabama advance to the Elite 8 for the second time in program history{{cite web |title=Alabama holds off top-seeded North Carolina 89-87 to reach Elite Eight for 2nd time ever |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401638632 |website=espn.com |publisher=AP |access-date=January 31, 2026 |date=March 29, 2024}} on their way to their first ever Final Four. On April 29, 2024, he announced he was returning for his final season at Alabama.{{cite news |last1=Byler |first1=Blake |title=Grant Nelson Returning to Alabama Basketball for Final Season |url=https://www.si.com/college/alabama/grant-nelson-returning-to-alabama-basketball-for-final-season |access-date=July 14, 2024 |work=Sports Illustrated |date=April 29, 2024}} In his final season of collegiate eligibility for [[2024–25 Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball team|Alabama]], he averaged 11.5 points, 7.6 rebounds, and 1.2 blocks per game, helping the Crimson Tide reach the Elite 8 as a 2-seed in the [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2025 NCAA Tournament]]. He was a huge factor in Alabama's overtime victory at [[Alabama–Auburn men's basketball rivalry|archrival]] [[2024–25 Auburn Tigers men's basketball team|Auburn]] in the final game of the regular season, scoring 23 points and grabbing 8 rebounds versus the Tigers.{{cite web |title=Mark Sears' floater at OT buzzer sends No. 7 Alabama past top-ranked Auburn 93-91 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401708437 |website=espn.com |publisher=AP |access-date=January 31, 2026 |date=March 8, 2025}} == Professional career == After going undrafted in the [[2025 NBA draft]], Nelson signed an [[Exhibit 10]] contract with the [[Brooklyn Nets]] to compete for a [[two-way contract]]. During the [[2025 NBA Summer League]], Nelson appeared in all five games and averaged 6.0 points, 4.4 rebounds and 1.2 assists in 19.1 minutes per game.{{Cite web |title=Brooklyn Nets Announce 2025 Summer League Roster {{!}} Brooklyn Nets |url=https://brooklynnets.com/news/brooklyn-nets-announce-2025-summer-league-roster |access-date=2025-10-15 |website=brooklynnets.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=Brooklyn Nets Sign Grant Nelson {{!}} Brooklyn Nets |url=https://brooklynnets.com/news/brooklyn-nets-sign-grant-nelson |access-date=2025-10-15 |website=brooklynnets.com |language=en}} On October 15, 2025, the Nets officially announced that they signed Nelson to a training camp deal,{{Cite web |title=Brooklyn Nets Sign Grant Nelson {{!}} Brooklyn Nets |url=https://brooklynnets.com/news/brooklyn-nets-sign-grant-nelson |access-date=2025-10-15 |website=brooklynnets.com |language=en}} but waived him on October 18.{{Cite web |date=2025-10-18 |title=Grant Nelson: Cut by Brooklyn |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/grant-nelson-cut-by-brooklyn/ |access-date=2025-10-18 |website=CBS Sports |language=en}} He later signed with the [[Long Island Nets]] of the [[NBA G League]] on November 3.{{Cite web |title=LONG ISLAND NETS ANNOUNCE TRAINING CAMP ROSTER |url=https://longisland.gleague.nba.com/news/long-island-nets-announce-training-camp-roster-6 |access-date=2025-11-20 |website=Long Island Nets |language=en}} On February 27, 2026, the Nets signed Nelson to a 10-day contract, where he saw his first NBA minutes. Across four appearances for Brooklyn, Nelson averaged 4.3 points, 1.5 rebounds, and 1.3 assists.{{Cite web |title=Grant Nelson ESPN |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/4702670/grant-nelson}} Following the expiry of his contract on March 9, the Nets elected not to re-sign Nelson.{{Cite web|title=Reports: Brooklyn Nets not re-signing Grant Nelson|url=https://www.devilslakejournal.com/sports/11084/reports-brooklyn-nets-not-re-signing-grant-nelson/|access-date=March 16, 2026|website=devilslakejournal.com|language=en}} On March 13, it was announced that Nelson had returned to Long Island; concurrently it was revealed that Brooklyn had not re-signed Nelson due to [[patellar tendinitis]] that would sideline him for the remainder of the season.{{Cite web|title=Malachi Smith earns Nets 10-day contract as Grant Nelson's season ends early|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/malachi-smith-earns-nets-10-183259302.html|access-date=March
